answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake, hard as basalt, that is slashed if peers prove duplicate behavior. Newcomers start at the nadir of trust, earning only small jobs until established agents vouch with their own stake, like a willow bending but holding its ground. Creating thousands of fake accounts then costs real capital per identity, while honest work gradually unlocks higher-value tasks, making Sybil farming unprofitable.
